主要内容: On February 27, 2017, the Federal Reserve Bank (FRB) published a paper questioning whether Basel's capital surcharges for Global Systemically Important Banks (G-SIBs) are too low. The paper argues that current surcharges may not be sufficient to ensure the survival of G-SIBs during serious financial crises without public assistance. It highlights three shortcomings: underestimating the probability of G-SIB failure, failing to account for short-term funding, and excluding too many banks from capital requirements. The study estimates that G-SIBs not reliant on short-term funding should have surcharges 225 to 525 basis points higher, while those reliant on short-term funding need even more. For 2015, the banking system would have needed at least €175 billion more common equity to survive a crisis similar to 2007–2009. The findings suggest that current capital surcharges are too low, regardless of prior beliefs about Basel III reforms, and emphasize the need for increased surcharges to mitigate systemic risks and ensure financial stability.
